prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: B042 is the one shortlisted candidate with a clean chain from idea to measurement: Kane and Mele predicted a time-reversal-protected spin Hall state and defined the Z2 invariant, and Molenkamp's group then observed the conductance of the helical edge channels in HgTe wells. Nearly twenty years of independent confirmation in 2D and 3D materials, including transport and ARPES, and the breadth of impact on materials, spintronics and quantum devices, make the discovery both original and mature. It has the most support in the opening round (five top-three placements, the highest Borda total), and I ranked it first for these reasons and not because of that support.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real. Bernevig, Hughes and the late Shoucheng Zhang made the HgTe proposal that Molenkamp's experiment tested, and Fu, Moore, Balents, Hsieh and Hasan are central to the 3D story. The three-name limit and Zhang's death mean the trio is a defensible compromise, not a complete account. The 2016 prize on topological phases also covers adjacent ground, and the quantisation of the quantum spin Hall edge is less clean than that of the quantum Hall effect, which weakens the experimental half.

responses.point: Ranked the optical lattice clock (B037) first as a clean, original, mature piece of precision measurement whose timing is good, perhaps overdue given the 2005 and 2012 prizes on adjacent topics.
responses.response: I agree that B037 is mature and attributable, and the two-name credit is better resolved than for B042, which is why I keep it as an alternative. I do not accept that the adjacent 2005 and 2012 prizes make it overdue. Ye already shared the 2005 prize, the clock builds on the comb and ion-trap precision that the Academy has recognised, and the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so the strongest practical payoff is still pending. As an instrument builder I value the engineering, but I see more novelty in a new class of matter than in a further improvement in accuracy.

responses.point: Placed the ATLAS and CMS Higgs discovery (B006) first as the experimental completion of the electroweak sector, left unrewarded after the 2013 theory prize, while admitting that attribution is the hard part.
responses.response: The science is beyond dispute, and I share your sense that the experimental discovery has no prize. My reservation is attribution. The names are founders and project leaders, but the discovery was made by the analysis teams and the thousands who built the detectors, and any three-person selection from two collaborations will be disputed. You say you would want expert input on whether detector leadership is the right proxy. I think that is a serious unresolved question, and until it is answered I cannot put B006 ahead of a candidate whose three names track decisive contributions, even with B042's credit gaps. I keep B006 as an alternative, not as my preference.

responses.point: Ranked B042 second, praising the chain from the Kane-Mele proposal through HgTe to edge transport, while stressing that Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D contributors are not all represented and suggesting a fair configuration might merge B042 with the overlapping B012.
responses.response: I share your credit concern, and it is the main weakness of my own first choice. I would not merge B012 into the configuration because B012 is not on the shortlist and the three-name limit would leave the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall stories fighting for the same places. I would keep the citation tied to the quantum spin Hall prediction and observation and say plainly that the 3D and BHZ contributions lie outside it. Your point about the less clean edge quantisation also seems fair to me and I would acknowledge it in the citation text.

responses.point: Ranked active-matter hydrodynamics (B005) first as one of the strongest conceptual advances in statistical physics, with a three-name credit mapping onto distinct contributions, though Yuhai Tu is omitted and the exact Toner-Tu exponents are debated.
responses.response: I find the conceptual case for B005 interesting, and your credit mapping is better than my B042 mapping. But the question that decides it for me is how directly the experiments test the theory. Giant number fluctuations are well tested, while the central Toner-Tu prediction of long-range order in 2D has not been tested well enough to call the theory settled, and you note that the exponents are still debated. The omission of Tu is also a substantive gap. B005 had a single first-place vote and no support among the other members, so I do not see a route for it to command a committee majority.

responses.point: Ranked B042 second and solid-state femtosecond lasers (B004) first, calling the invention clear and the impact broad, while noting that Kerr-lens priority is shared with others.
responses.response: I agree with you on B042, and your note that the HgTe theory is unrecognised matches my own. For B004 I am less convinced. The tools are indispensable, but ultrafast optics was recognised in 2018 with chirped pulse amplification and in 2023 with attosecond pulses, which used exactly these sources. Kerr-lens priority, which you and Kroll both flag as uncertain, also weakens the credit. I think B004 would look like a third prize in one cluster, whereas B042 has no immediate duplicate in the recent record apart from the 2016 prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept a trio that leaves out Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological insulator contributors, or would judge the credit too incomplete.
How much weight the 2016 topological-phase prize should carry against a quantum spin Hall prize.
Whether detector founders and project leaders are a defensible proxy for the ATLAS and CMS discovery (B006), which would change my ranking if resolved.
Whether Ye's earlier recognition and the pending redefinition of the second should move B037 above or below B042.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B042 or B037. My background includes CERN-based doctoral work and instrument-building collaborations in astroparticle physics (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+), which gives me a general affinity with experimental detector projects such as ATLAS and CMS (B006); no personal tie to those collaborations is recorded, but I will flag it for transparency and leave it to the committee to decide on recusal.
